source.title: The Ignition Index: Measuring Global Workspace Dynamics in Language Models

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses induction-head timing as context, but its own training-time results measure a probe-based Ignition Index, not induction-head formation, in-context learning, or the training loss pattern specified by the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports architecture, signal-strength, and training-checkpoint results for its Ignition Index. These are not measurements of induction behaviour or in-context learning as specified in the claim. The cited induction-head formation timing is from prior work and is not a result of this study.
record.test_reason: The study measures a probe-based Ignition Index (sigmoid steepness of layer-wise linguistic probe accuracy). It does not measure induction heads, prefix-matching or copying scores, in-context learning, or the loss bump. The induction-head step (≈2,000) it compares against is cited from Olsson et al., not measured. Its results bear on no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors report a significant Ignition Index changepoint at step 256 in Pythia-410M, which they say precedes cited induction-head formation (~2,000), possibly a distinct earlier phase. They report no changepoint in Pythia-1.4B, with volatile early values they attribute to fitting artefacts. They call H4 (a discontinuity at induction-head formation) partially confirmed for the smaller model, even though the detected changepoint does not occur at the induction-head step.
record.recipe_differences: The study probes layer-wise linguistic information and fits sigmoid curves to derive an Ignition Index; it does not apply the original induction-head or in-context-learning measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Training dynamics differ by model: Pythia-410M has a detected changepoint, whereas Pythia-1.4B does not. The authors also note that Pythia-1.4B’s early extreme values may be fitting artefacts.

fits_no_version.finding: Pythia-410M shows an Ignition Index changepoint at step 256 (39.57→66.02). Pythia-1.4B shows no changepoint and near-zero values from step 4,000. The authors compare these with the cited induction-head step of ≈2,000.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layer-wise probe-accuracy steepness (Ignition Index) shifts during early Pythia training, before the cited induction-head formation step, with trajectories differing by model size.

record.problems: The training analysis uses N = 200 sentences per probing task per checkpoint. The authors note wide confidence intervals and likely sigmoid-fitting artefacts for some extreme early Pythia-1.4B values. Induction-head timing is cited from prior work rather than measured in this study.
record.rows_left_out: Architecture, signal-strength, and other Ignition Index results are omitted because they do not measure induction behaviour or in-context learning. The induction-head formation step used for comparison is cited from prior work, not measured here.

untested.parts: All: composition with a previous-token head and the [A][B]…[A]→[B] mechanism.
All: induction-head formation timing, ICL gain, loss bump. The ≈step 2,000 timing is cited only.
All. Induction behaviour is not measured in any of the 12 models.
All. The step-256 Ignition Index changepoint is not a sub-step of induction-head formation as measured here.

record.verdict_notes: H4 predicted a jump in the Ignition Index at induction-head formation. Neither model shows a changepoint near step 2,000. That is a result about the Ignition Index, not about induction heads. Induction heads are never identified or measured. The training analysis uses N=200 sentences per task, and some checkpoint values (e.g. ~300 at step 1,000) are acknowledged as likely fitting artefacts.

versions.untested_parts: Induction-head composition with a previous-token head and the [A][B] … [A] → [B] copying mechanism.

Induction-head formation, in-context-learning gain, and the training-loss bump are not measured; the paper measures a different metric and compares its timing with a cited induction-head formation step.
The contribution of induction heads to most in-context learning in large transformers.
Whether induction behaviour occurs across model families, sizes, runs, architectures, or modalities.
Dependence of induction-head formation or in-context learning on data and training setup.
Whether few-shot task learning is mainly carried by mechanisms other than induction heads.
Whether induction-head formation itself consists of several sub-steps or overlapping transitions.

rows.subject: Pythia-410M
rows.operation_detail: Measured the Ignition Index β̂ across training checkpoints and applied PELT changepoint analysis.

conditions.value: N = 200 sentences per probing task at each checkpoint

rows.measure: Training-time changepoint in Ignition Index β̂
rows.value: At step 256, β̂post = 66.02 (+67%); PELT detected a significant changepoint.
rows.note: This is a change in the paper’s Ignition Index, not a measurement of induction heads, in-context learning, or training loss. The comparison to induction-head timing is contextual; that timing is cited from prior work.
rows.check: This is an Ignition Index changepoint in Pythia-410M, not induction-head formation or ICL. It cannot show any version's effect, so the state should not be 'observed'. Baseline and value are read correctly (39.57→66.02 at step 256).

rows.subject: Pythia-1.4B
rows.operation_detail: Measured the Ignition Index β̂ across training checkpoints and applied PELT changepoint analysis.

conditions.value: N = 200 sentences per probing task at each checkpoint

rows.measure: Training-time changepoint in Ignition Index β̂
rows.value: No significant PELT changepoint detected; β̂ was highly volatile, with values near zero from step 4,000 onward.
rows.uncertainty: Wide BCa confidence intervals are noted for extreme early values; exact intervals not stated here.
rows.note: The authors describe early extreme values as likely sigmoid-fitting artefacts. This is a result about the Ignition Index, not induction-head formation or in-context learning.
rows.check: No PELT changepoint in the Ignition Index for Pythia-1.4B. This measures a different construct, so 'absent' relative to any version is not meaningful.
